Before: Secure-aggregation protocols differ in how clients exchange the information needed to combine updates. Bonawitz et al. (2017) presented a practical protocol. Bell et al. Their proofs assume that client corruptions are fixed before execution and that dropout stays within specified bounds. (2022) described Salvia, a SecAgg(+) implementation for Flower under a semi-honest model. In this model, participants follow the protocol but may try to learn from what they observe.
